notes: Both configurations achieved 100% pass rate across all 3 evals — no discriminating assertions found in this iteration.
The skill adds ~949 tokens and ~1.1s on average, a negligible overhead from reading the SKILL.md file.
Eval 2 (Incomplete Lying) was the most discriminating scenario — both caught the lie, but the baseline was equally capable at file-existence checks.
Eval 3 (Deviations) was equally well-handled by both — the model naturally compares plan names to code names regardless of skill guidance.

The with_skill report for Eval 2 used stronger language ('Dishonest', 'Critical Finding') and more structured formatting (explicit Missing files section), suggesting the skill encourages more rigorous presentation.

Current assertions may be too easy — they check for detection of obvious issues (missing files, wrong names) that Claude handles well without guidance. Harder scenarios (subtle logic bugs, partial implementations that look complete, performance issues) might differentiate skill value better.

Qualitative difference: the with_skill reports follow the SKILL.md template more closely (Implementation Status, Automated Verification, Code Review Findings, Manual Testing, Recommendations), while without_skill reports vary in structure but still contain equivalent information.
